label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
**Lee — the dumper numbers**

Right, I've done the sums on the tracked dumper so you can read it rather than me going on at you in the van.

**What we've been doing**
Hired the tracked dumper off the place in Sittingbourne, 14 days this year. £85 a day plus £30 delivery each time, so roughly £1600 all in. That's before fuel, and before the hours we spend loading and unloading the thing.

**What it costs to buy**
Bloke in Faversham's got a 2019, 500kg tracked one, £1650 ono, new tracks fitted last spring. Halves is **£825 each**. It'd live in my lean-to at the yard — it's covered and dry.

**How we'd split the running costs**
- Fuel and day-to-day running: 50/50 on every job we use it on.
- Servicing and repairs: 50/50.
- Whoever breaks it pays for that one. Only fair way round it.
- If it goes wrong and we hire a replacement for a job, we split that 50/50 too.

**Why it adds up**
- Three patio digs and the Boughton drive are already booked for spring, so it'll be working straight away.
- Last September the hire place didn't have one, so we ended up barrowing 6 ton of muck at the Hernhill job. Two extra days on the job and your back was gone for a week. That's what happens when we depend on them — with our own one, it can't happen.
- Even the delivery driver turning up at 11 one morning cost us half a morning.
- At this year's use it pays for itself in about a year. At half that use, about two years. Both before servicing and repairs, so it only gets better.
- If it doesn't work out we sell it on. Tracked dumpers hold their value and this one's got newish tracks. Not money wasted.

**Before we commit** — a few things I'll sort: covering it on my tools policy, how we shift it if it's not road registered, and what licence and training we both need so we're legal on site. None of that's a deal-breaker but I want it checked, not guessed at.

**Can you come and look at it with me on Saturday?** I'd rather we both saw it, ran it and checked it over before we commit. First come first served and I'd sooner it was us than someone else. Say 10am at mine, we'll go over to Faversham together.

£825 to get on the job instead of £1600 a year and climbing, Lee. Worth half an hour of your time on Saturday.
